text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A five-year-old child was killed and 99 houses were burnt down, leaving nearly 500 people homeless in a residential area of Ho Chi Minh City.
-- Some 140,000 tonnes of rice have been exported through Saigon Port so far this month and preparations are under way to export a further 120,000 tonnes to the Philippines and Malaysia.

-- The first Isuzu trucks produced locally by Isuzu-Vietnam Joint Venture will be marketed in May this year. The Joint Venture has an investment capital of $50 million, with 70 percent contributed by the Japanese partner.
-- Vice Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong received Japan's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Kazuo Ogura, who led a delegation of economic experts.
-- National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh received outgoing British ambassador Peter Williams.
-- A drive is under way to eliminate illiteracy in the central highlands province of Dac Lak by 1999, which now stands at a rate of 12.8 percent.

-- An economic conference between senior officials from Vietnam and Japan was held in Hanoi on Tuesday. Delegates focused on investment and trading. Vietnam's Vice Minister of Planning and Investment, Vo Hong Phuc, and Japan's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazuo Ogura chaired the conference.
